L8: # BlueROV2cite2† L9: 
L10: ## Descriptioncite3† L11: 
L12: An implementation of the BlueROV2 Heavy vehicle from Blue Robotics.
L13: 
L14: See the cite4†`BlueROV2` .
L15: ## Control Schemescite5† L16: 
L17: AUV Thrusters (``0``)
L18: 
L19: 
L20: An 8-length floating point vector used to specify the control on each thruster. They begin with the front right vertical thrusters, then goes around counter-clockwise, then repeat the last four with the sideways thrusters.
L21: 
L22: PID Controller (``1``)
L23: A 6-length floating point vector of desired position in the global frame and roll, pitch, and yaw. A basic PID controller is implemented to move the vehicle to that position and orientation using the needed forces and torques.
L24: 
L25: Custom Dynamics (``2``)
L26: A 6-length floating point vector of linear and angular accelerations in the global frame. This is to be used for implementing custom dynamics. Besides collisions, all other forces and torques (including gravity, buoyancy, and damping) have been disabled in the simulator to allow for a clean slate for custom dynamics.
L27: ## Socketscite6† L28: 
L29: All sockets have standard orientation unless stated otherwise. Standard orientation has the x-axis pointing towards the front of the vehicle, the y-axis pointing starboard, and the z-axis pointing upwards.
L30: ### Socket Definitionscite7† L31: 
L32:   * `COM` Center of mass.
L33: 
L34:   * `SonarSocket` Location of the sonar sensor.
L35: 
L36:   * `DVLSocket` Location of the DVL.
L37: 
L38:   * `IMUSocket` Location of the IMU. Rotated 180 on x-axis, i.e. in a NED frame instead of NWU.
L39: 
L40:   * `DepthSocket` Location of the depth sensor.
L41: 
L42:   * `CameraSocket` Location of the camera.
L43: 
L44:   * `Origin` True center of the robot.
L45: 
L46:   * `Viewport` Where the robot is viewed from.
L47: 
L48: ### Socket Framescite8† L49: ## Flashlightscite9† L50: 
L51: The BlueROV2 comes with four built-in flashlights positioned around the vehicle to provide illumination in various directions.
L52: 
L53:   * flashlight1: (22, 19, 11)
L54: 
L55:   * flashlight2: (22, -19, 11)
L56: 
L57:   * flashlight3: (22, 19, -6)
L58: 
L59:   * flashlight4: (22, -19, -6)
L60: 
L61: Please refer to cite10†flashlights for information on available control commands.

L39@P1: 1 Introduction
L40@P1: Texas Instruments has a large portfolio of DC/DC converters which operate over a wide range of input and
L41@P1: output voltages. However, the data sheet provides efficiency curves only at certain operating conditions.
L42@P1: The same device may be used at different output voltages, and the user may need to know the efficiency
L43@P1: or power dissipation at those output voltages. This application report explains how to calculate the
L44@P1: dissipated power at any output voltage and thereby plot the efficiency of the converter at any output
L45@P1: voltage. This provides a quick and easy method to obtain the power supply's efficiency without the need to
L46@P1: make laboratory measurements.
L47@P1: The three main causes of power dissipation in a DC/DC converter are:
L48@P1: • Inductor conduction losses
L49@P1: • MOSFET conduction losses
L50@P1: • MOSFET switching losses

L275@P5: Revision History
L276@P5: 5 Conclusion
L277@P5: This application report provides a quick and easy method to calculate the efficiency of a buck converter at
L278@P5: conditions other than what is provided by the data sheet. This procedure provides accurate results and
L279@P5: eliminates the need to build and test the power supply to get the efficiency data.
